$comment: Necessary but not sufficient: decimal bounds (x-gie-*), canonical order, cross-field invariants (x-gie-invariants), lifecycle rules (x-gie-behaviour), exact 64-bit integer tokens and printable-text rules are enforced by the reference implementation gie.contracts.

Contribution.description: Share of an estimate attributed to one driver (explainability).

evidence_id.description: Contributing evidence, or null for a named feature.

feature.description: Contributing feature from the feature dictionary, or null for evidence.

weight_r.description: Signed contribution to the expected net R.

x-gie-invariants.rule: exactly one of evidence_id and feature is set

PriceCondition.description: Observable price condition: the basis price compared with a level.

timeframe.description: Candle timeframe when basis is CANDLE_CLOSE, otherwise null.

trigger.description: Comparison that makes the condition true.

x-gie-invariants.rule: timeframe is a candle timeframe if and only if basis is CANDLE_CLOSE

Target.description: A profit destination of the plan.

close_frac.description: Share of the initial volume to close at this target (0 = no scheduled close).

scenario.description: Scenario of the candidate's destination this target is: the destination (scenario, label) of the plan's candidate, with the same price.  Null when the target is not one of the candidate's predicted destinations.

description: Executable plan: entry, hard stop, destinations, expected net R and uncertainty.

as_of_time_ns.description: Market-data watermark: receive time of the newest market data the record depends on, directly or through its inputs.

baseline_r.description: Part of expected_net_r not attributed to a contribution.

candidate_id.description: Candidate (one scorer's view) this plan was built from.

contributions.description: Attribution of expected_net_r to evidence and features.

data_origin.description: Least trustworthy origin among the market data the record is derived from.

decision_time_ns.description: Clock reading at which the producer created the record.

entry_order_type.description: Order type used for the entry.

entry_price.description: Intended entry level: the limit or stop-trigger price, or the retest / pullback level. Null only for entry style MARKET.

entry_trigger.description: Observable condition that must occur before the entry is attempted (e.g. the confirmation of a retest); null when none.

expected_cost_r.description: Expected spread, commission and slippage already deducted in expected_net_r.

expected_net_r.description: Expected net result in R of this plan's own risk distance.

invalidations.description: Observable conditions that invalidate the plan before entry (actual behaviour overrides the expectation); evaluated by the decision engine, which then emits a WITHDRAWN revision.

max_entry_slippage.description: Largest acceptable adverse difference between intended and achievable entry price.

max_spread.description: Do not enter while the spread is wider than this.

mode.description: REPLAY or PAPER.  No live mode exists (routing lock).

model_status.description: Promotion status of that model at decision time (only ACTIVE is validated).

model_version_id.description: Model (or rule set) version behind the estimates.

net_r_stdev.description: Outcome dispersion of a single result.

opportunity_id.description: Stable identity of the opportunity (same as on the candidate).

overnight_allowed.description: Whether the position may be held past the daily rollover (never over a weekend).

producer.description: Component instance that emitted the record; together with the contract name it names the stream.

reference_price.description: Executable price at decision time: ask for BUY, bid for SELL.

revision.description: 0 for the first record, +1 per update.

run_id.description: Run that produced the record (see the RunManifest of that run).

schema_version.description: Version of the contract the message was written with.

seq.description: Position of the record in its stream: starts at 0 and increases by exactly 1.

status_reasons.description: Why the plan was rejected or withdrawn.

stop_price.description: Hard protective stop.  In later revisions it may move towards the entry, never away from it.

supersedes_plan_id.description: Previous revision replaced by this record; null for revision 0.

support_count.description: Effective number of cases behind it.

symbol.description: Always XAUUSD: GIE trades only gold.

valid_until_ns.description: Expiry instant: the plan must not be acted on at or after it.  It is not later than the expiry of its candidate.

variant.description: Distinguishes several plans of the same entry style.

title: TradePlan 1.0.0

monotonic: stop_price never moves away from the entry between revisions
the risk distance |entry_price - stop_price| of a plan whose entry style is not MARKET never increases between revisions

x-gie-invariants.rule: as_of_time_ns <= decision_time_ns (a record cannot depend on data received after it was created)
plan_id equals identity.plan_id(candidate_id, entry_style, variant, revision)
entry_price is null if and only if entry_style is MARKET
entry styles MARKET, LIMIT and STOP use the order type of the same name; RETEST and PULLBACK use LIMIT or MARKET
the stop is on the losing side of the effective entry (BUY: stop < entry, SELL: stop > entry)
every target is on the winning side of the effective entry
the target close fractions sum to at most 1
when status is PREPARED, ARMED or SELECTED, valid_until_ns is later than decision_time_ns
status_reasons is non-empty when status is REJECTED or WITHDRAWN
supersedes_plan_id is null for revision 0 and otherwise equals the id of the previous revision, identity.plan_id(candidate_id, entry_style, variant, revision - 1)
an ARMED or SELECTED plan has expected_net_r > 0 (positive expectancy gate)
the plan states its uncertainty: net_r_stdev or expected_net_r_stderr
entry_trigger and every invalidation of a plan are prices greater than zero

while the plan is PREPARED, ARMED or SELECTED its resting entry lies beyond the market it was planned against: with order type LIMIT a BUY entry_price <= reference_price and a SELL entry_price >= reference_price; with order type STOP a BUY entry_price >= reference_price and a SELL entry_price <= reference_price
no two targets have the same (scenario, label)
